title: Iron, Bronze Mountains, and the Purpose of Divine Anger
english: Iron, as one who most strictly reproves God for being unyielding and having the appearance of a harlot, and for having shamed everyone and not submitting oneself to the gentle yoke of Jesus (Matthew 11:30): 'I know that you are hard; and your forehead is bronze, and the sinew of your neck is iron.'

Two bronze mountains are said to exist because of the twofold nature of those exalted against the knowledge of God. For it is possible to hold false opinions regarding both practical and intellectual virtue, not being any other than the knowledge of truth; for those from the heresies are impious concerning both kinds of virtue.

Regarding the black horses coming from the north as vessels of wrath (Revelation 6:8), 'from which the evils are burned upon those dwelling on the earth,' white horses were shown coming after them. These are the ministers of propitiation and of joy, and of profitable things. Since punishments are brought for the improvement of those surrendered to them, they follow harmoniously behind, clearly following them, weaving and announcing the bright and light-like things.

A soul, having experienced these, having become through perception, cries out most clearly toward that which approaches the destruction of the harmed (Micah 7:8): 'Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen; I shall rise again,' meaning, having repented. For even if, having fallen, I was cast down by punishment through the wrath of God, yet having endured and having bravely received the wrath that was incited, I have come into a propitiatory state and a rejoicing intercourse, saying: 'I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against Him, until He justifies my judgment (Psalm 119:71); and He will execute my judgment, and He will lead me out into the light, and I shall see His righteousness.'

For even if God is angered for the sake of improvement and benefit, He does not always do this; for He says: 'When the anger of the spirit arises, I will heal again.' He who has been benefited from such providence says gratefully to the one who has chastised for salvation by a little: 'I will bless You, Lord, that You were angry with me for salvation; You turned Your face and had mercy on me.'

When the black horses had come from the land of the north to rest the wrath of the Lord, the variegated and speckled were seen coming from the south; from that, namely, concerning which in the Song of Songs the bride says to her bridegroom: 'Come, south wind,' the cold north wind and harsh wind having been sent away by her. The bride's saying goes thus: 'Awake, north wind, and come, south wind; blow through my garden, and let my spices flow' (Song of Songs 4:16). And good words and pious thoughts are the spices. It was interpreted in what went before who the variegated horses are, and why they were so called. And all the horses stand by the Lord of all the earth, being ready to go around all the earth and to accomplish what the Lord of all the earth commands, or rather of all creation. The first tome having been circumscribed with regard to the visions of the prophet Zechariah, the brightly seeing one, we must begin the second from the following text, which goes thus. Tome 2. Zechariah 6:9-11: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Take from the captivity, from the rulers and from the useful ones of it and from those who have known it. And you shall enter on that day into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, who came from Babylon. And you shall take silver and gold and make crowns and set them upon the head of Jesus the son of Jozadak, the great priest. As it is not possible to speak or hand down scientific lessons without having science, so it is not possible to foreknow truly and according to God or to prophesy spiritual prophecy without the word of God coming to the one foreknowing and prophesying. For the word of the Lord, coming to such a one, gives eyes and illumines for beholding the beauties and mysteries of truth and of God's wisdom. And the word coming to the prophet is not other than the Word of God, who comes to holy men, both angels and principalities and authorities and thrones and dominions, being always toward the Father who begot him. For concerning the Father it is said that the Word was toward him: 'For this one,' it says, 'was toward God,' being God the Word (John 1:1-2). And he comes to be, and is not already, toward the spirit-bearing men, being also then toward them when he comes to be. For then they shall also be gods, toward whom he visited and came to be, as the Savior himself in the Gospel […]

title: The Spiritual Gold and Silver of Salvation
english: As if there are virtues and wise thoughts there. For having been benefited from the shameless and painful state, they acquired the good things about which it is said in the first song of the ascents toward the one blessed by the Lord: 'See the good things, Jerusalem' (Ps 122:2), and also: 'You shall trust in the Lord and He will bring you up to the good things of the earth', which is the inheritance given to those who learn from Jesus 'that He is gentle and humble in heart' (Matt 11:29). Concerning which the hymnist has cried out: 'I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living' (Ps 27:13). Similarly, also the blessed prophet Isaiah exhorts to take a desire for the interpreted good things: 'For if, he says, you wish and you listen to me, you may eat the good things of the earth' (Isa 1:19).

Having received the command from the captivity regarding this, having received it through the Word of the Lord having come to him, he is commanded to enter into the house of Josiah, who is receiving [the name] 'saving'. For it is fitting for the one being saved by the Lord, about whom it is written: 'Our God is a God of saving', having come 'to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10), to be a son of Zephaniah, interpreted as 'Jehovah is timing'. For a timing is being approached by God for the one having been saved with eternal salvation, of which the Savior is the cause, concerning which the Apostle writes concerning the Savior: 'Having been perfected, He became to all those obeying Him the cause of eternal salvation' (Hebrews 5:9).

To the one commanded to enter into the house of the one having come from Babylon into the holy city Jerusalem, a command is given to take silver and gold and to make crowns so that they may be placed on the head of the high priest, and this is Jesus, of the true Jesus being the salvation of God, receiving [the name] 'Salvation is Jehovah', meaning that of God; for one of the names of God is Jehovah in the Hebrew voice. Let us observe more of the gold and the silver from which crowns are constructed by the one having received the command. Silver is the word and gold is the mind, they are taken up by the law of allegory. For it is said in the Song of Songs concerning these being spiritual treasures for the bride by the friends of her bridegroom, the king being: 'I will make you likenesses of gold after a moment of silver, until the king reclines on his couch' (Song 1:11). title: Shadows and Spiritual Crowns
english: The writings before the arrival of the Savior are shadowy and iconic pedagogies; which the Apostle says are 'shadows of the things to come' (Colossians 2:17) and 'an image of the things hereafter attained' (Colossians 2:17); and these are the things to come, consisting according to the life-giving Spirit.

2.17 And since the likenesses of the said intelligible gold are varied and formed from the divinely inspired words, the likenesses of the intelligible gold receive their variety from the flakes of silver. What then is the silver from which the flakes decorate the likenesses of the gold, or is it 'the pure words of the Lord, being silver refined in a furnace on the earth' (Psalm 12:6)?

2.18 Concerning the said intelligible gold and the appropriate silver in that bridal chamber, it is said regarding the peaceful bridegroom: 'King Solomon made for himself a throne from the wood of Lebanon; he made for himself pillars of silver, and his canopy was gold' (1 Kings 10:18). Of this spiritual throne, the pillars are made of the aforementioned silver, and its canopy is inherently spiritual gold.

2.19 And since it happens that those striving for piety are shown to be victors from the said treasures, 'contending even unto death for the sake of truth' (2 Timothy 4:7), from them the crowns are constructed of the spiritual treasures, so that the martyrs of the truth and all those who have overcome the fleshly adversaries may be honored, having taken under their feet those called 'rulers, authorities, and cosmic powers of this darkness, spiritual evils' (Ephesians 6:12).

2.20 Since there are many and diverse combats, it is necessary that the prizes also be many and diverse. Therefore, not one but many crowns are crafted by him who has received the command. For every virtue and the works performed according to it has its own proper crown.

2.21 For he who has heard the laws of his Father God and 'has not rejected the statutes of his mother' (Galatians 4:26), 'the free Jerusalem above' (Galatians 4:26) and 'the glorious Church' (Ephesians 5:27), receives a 'crown of graces' upon his own head, being adorned with a 'golden garland' which decorates the submissive power of the soul, allegorically called the 'neck'.
